steps.body: Just like single equations, systems have three cases — and you can tell WHICH before solving by comparing the lines. DIFFERENT slopes → the lines cross → ONE solution. Same slope needs a closer look.

widget.prompt: How many solutions does the system y = 2x + 1 and y = 3x − 1 have?

options.label: One solution
options.feedback: Right — different slopes (2 and 3) mean the lines cross exactly once.

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: The no-solution case needs PARALLEL lines (equal slopes) — here the slopes differ (2 vs 3), so they cross once.

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: That needs the SAME line twice — here the slopes differ, so just one crossing.

options.label: Two solutions
options.feedback: Two straight lines cross at most once — different slopes give exactly one solution.

predict.prompt: Two lines with DIFFERENT slopes — how many times can they cross?
predict.reveal: Different tilts guarantee the lines drift together and apart at different rates — they meet at one single point and never again.

steps.body: When the slopes are EQUAL, the lines are parallel. If their y-intercepts DIFFER, they never meet — NO solution. If the y-intercepts are the SAME too, they're the same line — INFINITELY many solutions.

explanationVariants: y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x − 3 have equal slopes (2) but different intercepts (1 vs −3): parallel, no solution.
Same slope, different intercept → parallel → no solution.

widget.prompt: How many solutions does the system y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x − 3 have?

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: Right — equal slopes but different intercepts means parallel lines that never meet.

options.label: One solution
options.feedback: Equal slopes (both 2) make the lines parallel — they never cross, so no solution.

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: That needs the SAME intercept too — here they differ (1 vs −3), so no solution.

options.label: Two solutions
options.feedback: Parallel lines have zero crossings, not two — no solution.

widget.prompt: How many solutions does the system y = 4x + 2 and y = 4x + 2 have?

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: Right — identical equations describe the same line, so every point on it is a solution.

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: The lines are identical (same slope AND intercept), so they share every point — infinitely many, not none.

options.label: One solution
options.feedback: Being the exact same line means they overlap everywhere — infinitely many crossings, not one.

options.label: Zero
options.feedback: Identical lines share all their points, giving infinitely many solutions, not zero.

explanationVariants: y = x + 4 and y = x − 4: equal slopes (1), different intercepts (4 vs −4) — parallel, no solution.
Same slope, different intercept → no solution.

widget.prompt: How many solutions does the system y = x + 4 and y = x − 4 have?

options.label: No solution
options.feedback: Right — equal slopes, different intercepts: parallel lines, no crossing.

options.label: One solution
options.feedback: Equal slopes (both 1) make them parallel — no crossing, so no solution.

options.label: Infinitely many
options.feedback: The intercepts differ (4 vs −4), so they're distinct parallel lines: no solution.

options.label: x = 4
options.feedback: There's no crossing at all — parallel lines give no solution.

steps.body: A system's solution count comes from comparing slopes and intercepts.
takeaways: Same slope, different intercepts → no solution (parallel).
Same slope AND intercept → infinitely many (same line).

concept.body: A system's solution count: different slopes → one (lines cross); same slope, different intercepts → none (parallel); same slope AND intercept → infinitely many (same line).

explanationVariants: y = 3x + 2 and y = 5x − 1 have different slopes (3 vs 5), so they cross once — one solution.
Different slopes → one crossing → one solution.
